assignments.reason: Faith in the Sages (emunat chakhamim) is the specific, concrete expression of emunah in this Torah. Its essential nature is faith — the central theme of Package 1. The Torah states 'on-through the vow he returns to emunat chakhamim.' It is the TARGET of the faith-restoration process, not the vow itself, but its nature IS faith in the Sages. Already related to 'אמונה' and 'אין לו אמונת חכמים' in Package 1.

Restoring fallen faith (lehaqim emunah ha-nefulah) is essentially the PROCESS of faith-restoration. Its nature is emunah — the core domain of Package 1. The Torah frames this as the central practical goal: 'tiqquno — she-yaqim emunah ha-nefulah.' Though it appears as an eitza-effect of Yaakov/neder, the concept itself IS about faith.

The lights of the Patriarchs (he'arot ha-avot) are the spiritual illumination emanating from Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov. Their essential nature IS the Patriarchs — the avot domain. Package 1 already contains 'אבות' and 'אות שין' (= Patriarchs). He'arot ha-avot is the active radiance of the same Patriarchal domain.

This is a variant expression of 'he'arot ha-avot' — the lights of the Patriarchs ('these lights' refers to orot ha-avot from section 3-4). Same essential nature as the Patriarchal lights domain in Package 1.

The sparkling of the Patriarchal light upon a person (mitnoztzetzim orot ha-avot) describes the Patriarchs' light becoming active in someone. Its essential nature is the Patriarchal illumination domain — the same as avot/shin in Package 1. It is an EFFECT of neder, but what it IS is Patriarchal light.

assignments.node_id: כשנתתקן הידים הנ"ל על ידי נדר כנ"ל, על ידי זה מתנוצצים בו אורות האבות
assignments.reason: This long-form node describes the effect of the vow restoring the angel-hands and thereby sparking Patriarchal lights. Despite its verbose form, the core concept described IS the neder-to-orot-ha-avot causal chain — both elements (neder, avot) belong to Package 1. The node's essential nature is the Yaakov/neder/avot nexus.

The Sages of the generation (chakhmei ha-dor) are the living bearers of Torah wisdom to whom faith is directed. Their essential nature IS the Sages — the same domain as 'emunat chakhamim' and 'histalkut ha-chakhamim' (departure of the Sages) in Package 1. The Torah teaches that healing depends on the Sages' ability to interpret Torah; disbelieving them removes healing. Chakhmei ha-dor ARE the Sages whose concealment = pele.

The opening of the gates of holiness (niftachim sharei ha-kedusha) is the cosmic result of faith being restored. Its essential nature is the holy-gates domain — the positive counterpart to the evil gates (shaar aram, Package 5). However, the concept of these gates opening is directly tied to emunah: 'pitchu she'arim... shomer emunim.' The gates of holiness open BECAUSE of faith. Their nature is the holy/faith domain of Package 1, as the mirror-structure of the Torah connects faith (Pkg 1) to the fall of the evil gate (Pkg 5).

Torah (ba-Torah) as the source of all healing. In Torah #57, Torah is not a separate thematic domain but is mediated entirely through the Sages — 'the Torah was given to them to interpret through the 13 hermeneutic principles.' Torah's role here is inseparable from emunat chakhamim. Without faith in the Sages, Torah's healing power is inaccessible. Its essential nature in THIS Torah is the Sages/faith domain of Package 1.

Healing/remedies (refu'ot) in this Torah are entirely dependent on faith in the Sages. The Torah's opening argument is: 'all refu'ot depend on the Torah' and 'one who damages emunat chakhamim has no healing.' Refu'ot's essential nature in this Torah IS the faith-in-Sages system — it is what becomes available when faith is intact and inaccessible when faith is absent. It belongs with the emunah domain of Package 1.

The power of healing received from the Torah (koach ha-refu'ah she-meqablin me-ha-Torah) is the specific mechanism: Torah gives power to angels, angels give power to herbs, herbs heal. But the key teaching is that this power is ONLY accessible through the Sages of the generation, who know how to compound (leharkiv) the Torah's letters. The concept's essential nature is the Torah-Sages-healing nexus, which is the emunah/chakhamim domain of Package 1.

This is a spelling variant of 'ענג שבת' which is already the dominant node of Package 3. The node_id in the edge uses the full-vowel form 'עונג שבת' vs. the defective spelling 'ענג שבת' in the package. Same concept — Shabbat delight. Belongs to Package 3.

The delight of Shabbat eating (oneg akilat Shabbat) is the specific act of eating in holiness on Shabbat. Its essential nature IS Shabbat delight — the core of Package 3. Package 3 already contains 'ענג שבת' and 'אכילה'; this node combines both into a single expression of the same Shabbat-eating domain.

Rising and delighting in Shabbat delight (oleh u-mit'aneg be-oneg Shabbat) describes the experiential state of accessing Shabbat pleasure. Its essential nature IS Shabbat delight — the same domain as Package 3's core.

Shabbat eating (akilat Shabbat) is the concrete act of eating on Shabbat. Its essential nature is Shabbat holy eating — Package 3 already contains 'אכילה' and 'ענג שבת'. Akilat Shabbat is the specific combination. The Torah states: 'akilat Shabbat kodesh hi' — Shabbat eating IS holiness.
At the time of Shabbat eating (bi-sh'at akilat Shabbat) — this is a temporal expression of the same Shabbat-eating concept. Its essential nature is Shabbat eating, the core domain of Package 3.

The completion of speech unto peace (nishlam ha-dibbur le-shalom) is the state where speech reaches its fullness in creating peace. Its essential nature IS speech/dibbur — the defining quality of the matzah/heh/five-mouth-positions domain of Package 2. The Torah contrasts 'shalom she-ein lo peh' (Package 4) with the shalom that HAS speech — the speech dimension is what distinguishes matzah-peace from chametz-peace. The dibbur-le-shalom belongs with the speech/koach-ha-dibbur domain.

The mouth is completed in great light (ha-peh nishlam be-or gadol) describes the perfection of the mouth/speech faculty during Shabbat eating. Its essential nature IS the mouth/peh/speech domain — Package 2's core concepts are the five articulatory positions of the mouth (chameshset motzaot ha-peh) and koach ha-dibbur. The peh being completed in light IS the power-of-speech domain.

Charity to the poor (tzedakah la-aniyim) is the means by which peace is amplified. The Torah states: 'marbeh tzedakah marbeh shalom' and 'shemesh be-Shabbat tzedakah la-aniyim.' Tzedakah's essential nature in this Torah is inseparable from the Shabbat-sun-peace triad. It is the mechanism that turns the Shabbat's enemy-subduing power into fullness of peace. Package 3 contains shemesh and shalom; tzedakah is the connector that completes that domain.

Fasting or Shabbat eating (tzom o akilat Shabbat) as a compound concept describes the two paths to subduing enemies. While it includes fasting (Package 4), the combined expression represents the general category of enemy-subduing practices, and the Torah presents Shabbat eating as the higher, preferred path. As a combined node, its primary domain is the Shabbat-and-peace framework of Package 3, since the Torah's culmination is that Shabbat eating achieves what fasting achieves and more.

assignments.node_id: צום או אכילת שבת לבד. אבל לרב השלום, צריך גם להרבות בצדקה
assignments.reason: This long-form node describes the teaching that fasting/Shabbat eating alone subdue enemies, but for ABUNDANT peace one must also give charity. Its essential nature is the Shabbat-peace-charity triad — the core of Package 3's shalom domain. The concept teaches about levels of peace, which IS the peace (shalom) domain.

Enemies falling before him (oyvav noflim le-fanav) describes the DEFEAT of enemies. The enemies themselves are the Esav/Edom/liver complex. The concept 'oyvav noflim' is about the enemies — the evil forces (meqatregim, shultanei rugzin) that emanate from the kaved/Esav. Their falling is a state of THOSE enemies. The essential nature of this node is the evil-domain enemies, which IS Package 5. The falling is what happens TO them, but they ARE the evil forces.

Annulling and subduing the enemies (she-levatel u-lehakhnia ha-oyvim) describes the subjugation of the evil forces. Like 'oyvav noflim,' the essential subject is the enemies themselves — the Esav/kaved/meqatregim forces of Package 5. The concept IS about those evil forces and what happens to them.

assignments.node_id: להפיל אויביו לפניו, בזכות ענג שבת, כמו שפועל בצום
assignments.reason: Causing enemies to fall through Shabbat delight, as fasting accomplishes — this long-form node describes the defeat of the evil forces. Despite mentioning Shabbat/fasting as the means, the essential subject is the ENEMIES FALLING. The enemies are the evil domain of Package 5.

The gate of Aram falls once (nofel sha'ar Aram pa'am achat) — this is the first collapse of the evil gate. Its essential nature IS the gate of Aram/sitra achra — the evil-gate domain already in Package 5 (shaar aram, shaar de-sitra achra). The falling is an event affecting that evil gate.

The liver is subdued before the brain (nikna ha-kaved lifnei ha-moach) — the essential subject is the KAVED being subdued. The kaved IS the dominant node of Package 5 (Esav/Edom/liver). This describes what happens to the kaved — it is humbled. The concept's nature is the liver/evil domain.

The repair of anger (tikkun ha-ka'as) is the corrective process for anger through fasting. Package 4 already contains 'תקון הכעס על ידי התענית' — the full form of this concept. Tikkun ha-ka'as is a shortened reference to the same concept. Its essential nature is the fasting/chametz/anger-repair domain of Package 4, which represents the partial tikkun path.

assignments.node_id: אין צריך לצום (יב). כי פועל באכילתו, מה שפעל על־ידי הצום, הינו להשבית אויב. כי אכילת שבת, קדש היא, "וכל זר לא יאכל קדש" (ויקרא כ"ב). ואז נכנע הכבד, ואז נתבטל כחו, בבחינת (תרומה קל"ה:): וכל שולטני רגזין, שהם בחינת כבד כועס, כלהו ערקין ואתעברו*. ואז וכלא אהבה, בבחינת (שיר־השירים ז): "אהבה בתענוגים", וכל זה מענג שבת הנ"ל
assignments.reason: This long-form node describes the state of not needing to fast because Shabbat eating accomplishes the same enemy-subduing result. Its essential teaching is about the superiority of oneg Shabbat — the core concept of Package 3. Despite mentioning the kaved and shultanei rugzin, the node's PRIMARY assertion is about oneg Shabbat's power.

assignments.node_id: מכניע את הכבד, ונותן הממשלה להמח. וכשנכנע הכבד, שהוא ראש המקטרגים, אזי נכנעים כל האויבים האחוזים בהכבד
assignments.reason: This long-form node describes the mechanism of fasting: subduing the liver and giving dominion to the brain, causing all enemies attached to the liver to be subdued. It is an EFFECT of fasting (ta'anit, Package 4). While it mentions the kaved (Package 5), the node describes the PROCESS that fasting achieves — this is the ta'anit mechanism. Its essential nature is the fasting-tikkun domain of Package 4.

assignments.node_id: מתקן את פניו, ומחזיר לעצמו את חכמתו, שהיא צלמו המאיר בפניו. ואז הכל יראים ממנו, ואויביו נופלים לפניו.
assignments.reason: This long-form node describes how fasting repairs one's face and restores one's wisdom/divine-image, causing enemies to fall. It is another description of the MECHANISM of fasting's effect. The essential nature is the fasting-tikkun process — returning the tzelem to the face through fasting. This is the core corrective action of the chametz/ta'anit domain (Package 4).

assignments.node_id: נכנע הכבד לפני המח, והגדלה והממשלה להמח. וזהו תקון למה שפגם בתחלה בהחכמה, שהיא המח, שהיא הצלם המאיר בפניו.
assignments.reason: This long-form node elaborates on the liver being subdued before the brain and the resulting repair of wisdom/tzelem. It is a detailed description of fasting's mechanism. Its essential nature is the fasting-corrective domain of Package 4.

assignments.node_id: זוכה לשבת, להשבית אויב, וזוכה לשלום כנ"ל. ואז נבנה פעם שלישי שער דקדשה, בבחינת (זכריה א): "ומשפט שלום שפטו בשעריכם". ובבחינת צדקה, "אל תדכא עני בשער" (משלי כ"ב). ומכניעים השונאים היונקים משער ארם
assignments.reason: This long-form node describes meriting Shabbat, achieving peace, building the third gate of holiness, and subduing enemies who feed from the gate of Aram. Its essential nature is the Shabbat-peace-gates-of-holiness domain. While it mentions shaar Aram (Package 5), the PRIMARY subject is the positive achievement of Shabbat and shalom — the domain of Package 3.
